title: Private deployment resiliency sentinel and safe-rollback runbook
creator: Aisha Khatri
description: Create a robust runbook and automated remediation flow (Sentinel) for common Private (VPC) health-check failures caused by Terraform/IaC drift, upgrade-induced config mismatch, and network glue issues. The goal is to reduce MTTR for private nodes from operator-led manual fixes (~45m) to automated safe mitigation (<10m) with clear audit trails and non-destructive rollback guards.
background: Private deployments periodically experience degraded health checks in two common patterns: (1) control-plane/agent disconnects after node image or runtime upgrades; (2) network misconfigurations from Terraform drift (route table, NAT, or security group changes) that break health-probe connectivity.

Existing artifacts focus on terraform-driven remediation and node autorepair but do not include a compact, operator-friendly sentinel with a safe-apply / dark-run pattern and explicit fallback to hosted inference for critical customer traffic.
This ticket bundles a runbook, automation scripts (safe-terraform-plan+apply saga), and gating rules for canary upgrades across private pools.

Primary risk: automated terraform apply on customer VPCs — mitigated with strict plan validation, operator approval flow, and no-destructive-change assertion rules. All changes must be logged and attached to the Linear ticket and runtime audit logs.
acceptance_criteria: A readable runbook exists in JSON that operators can follow to identify, diagnose, and remediate the 5 top failure modes (agent crash, heartbeat loss, route drift, NAT egress outage, KV-cache mismatch).
A safe automation flow (playbook) can perform a non-destructive terraform dry-run, present a highlighted diff, and apply only when automated assertions pass or an assignee confirms.
Automated remediation reduces median MTTR for health-check failures in the staging fleet by >= 60% in the controlled test harness.
All remediation actions emit audit log events with a link to the terraform plan and the Linear ticket ID.
Feature flag 'private.auto_remediate' can be toggled per-customer and defaults to off for high-compliance customers.
Postmortem template and follow-up tasks for any automated remediation that required manual escalation are created and linked.
runbook_triggers: Private Node Health-check failed >=3 consecutive probes within 2 minutes
Terraform drift detector reports >1 resource drift in private cluster module
KV cache errors rate > 5% for inference runtime in the node logs
Route table target unreachable for private-subnet probe endpoint
diagnostics_checks: Check node agent logs: kubectl -n redwood logs node-agent-<node> --tail=500
Check Terraform state drift: terraform -chdir=iac/private plan -detailed-exitcode
Network path test from control plane: iperf3/ traceroute to probe endpoint and 8.8.8.8 to validate NAT egress
automated_remediation_flow: Step 1: Isolate impact — mark node as maintenance to stop new inference traffic (api->route table override).
Step 2: Run non-destructive checks: terraform plan (exit codes), dry-run of runtime config validate, and network path smoke tests.

Step 3: If terraform plan reports only non-disruptive drift (tags, metadata, autoscaling thresholds), automatically run a safe-apply with --target to only reconcile drifted resources. Otherwise, create operator approval workflow with highlights of changed resources.
Step 4: If node agent is unhealthy but network is ok, restart agent container and background services (systemctl restart redwood-agent || kubectl rollout restart daemonset/node-agent).

Step 5: If KV cache mismatch detected after runtime upgrade, trigger cache-clear job (redwood-cachectl clear --node <node> --models <list>) and warm prefix cache from peers using controlled warmup traffic.

Step 6: If network route/NAT is missing, and terraform has a single resource drift for route table or IGW/NAT gateway, run safe terraform apply using a pre-approved plan artifact and post-apply connectivity check.
Step 7: If automation cannot verify restore within timeout (10 minutes), mark remediation as partial and escalate to on-call SRE with full context and a pinned timeline.
safety_guards_and_assertions: All automated terraform applies run with a plan file stored in S3 and a checksum check. The apply job will fail if plan file changed since approval.
Disruptive change detection: block automation for any plan that modifies subnet CIDR, replaces NAT gateway, or deletes security groups. These require manual runbook steps.
Traffic preservation: nodes are cordoned before any risky actions and traffic is shifted with a gradual weight ramp to avoid request loss.
Operator confirmation required for > 3 resources changed or if change includes resource replacement. Confirmation captured as a signed entry in audit logs.
Feature flag per-customer for auto-remediate; default off for customers with compliance tag 'no_auto_remediate'.
runbook_steps: 1) Triage: gather node ID, last successful probe, and recent prometheus spikes. Link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/private/nodes?var-node=<node>
2) Run quick health checks (3m): agent logs, heartbeat, network path. Use diagnostic commands listed above.
3) Identify drift: run terraform plan and capture exit code. If exit code == 2 (changes), upload plan to s3 and attach to ticket.
4) Decide path: if changes are tagged non-disruptive and within safe-assertions, start automated apply. Otherwise follow manual remediation checklist.
5) Execute remediation: cordon node, apply fix, restart agent/runtime as necessary, run post-checks for 5 minutes.
6) Reintroduce node: uncordon and monitor 30m for probe stability and latency regressions. If regressions occur, rollback to previous runtime image via pinned release tag.
7) Post-incident: attach plan, logs, and evidence to ticket, run postmortem template if customer impact high.
rollback_steps: If apply introduced new failures, perform the following in order:
A) Revert terraform with stored plan reversal artifact: terraform apply -input=false -auto-approve <revert-plan>
B) Roll runtime image back: kubectl set image daemonset/node-agent redwood-agent=<previous-image-tag>
C) Restore route tables from snapshot using cloud-provider restore script and verify with traceroute
D) If KV cache clear caused issues, restore persisted KV snapshot and place node into read-only mode until consistency is verified.
monitoring_and_metrics: Track MTTR for private health-check failures (target <10m for automated cases)
Alert if automated remediation fails more than 1 in 10 runs in staging
Emit a remediation_event metric with tags: customer_id, node_id, trigger, remediation_result
Dashboard: Private / Remediation — shows recent plan diffs, apply success rate, and average time-to-restore
tests_and_validation: Staging harness: inject synthetic probe failures across 50 nodes and verify the automation restores >=95% within 10 minutes
Chaos test: simulate terraform state-lock and ensure plan/approval flow surfaces sensible error and does not auto-apply
Canary rollout: enable auto_remediate for 2 non-prod customers, monitor for 72 hours before widening
Security review: automated apply must pass internal KMS audit and least-privilege checks
